def: Storing weights, activations or cache entries with fewer bits by mapping each value to the nearest of a small set of allowed values.
The step size between neighbouring quantised levels, chosen so the largest value in a group maps to the largest integer.
Multiplying stored integers back by their scale to recover approximate real values before or during a matrix multiplication.
A scheme where the scale is the largest absolute value divided by the largest integer, so zero maps exactly to zero.
An integer offset in asymmetric quantisation that lets the integer range cover any interval, not only one centred on zero.
Using a separate scale for each output channel (row) of a weight matrix.
Using one scale for each run of 32 to 128 consecutive weights, which confines the damage of an outlier to its own group.
A few activation channels in large transformers whose values are far larger than the rest and that make low-precision activation quantisation hard.
A method that divides activation channels by a factor and multiplies the matching weight rows by it, moving quantisation difficulty from activations to weights.
A post-training method that quantises weights one at a time and updates the remaining weights using second-order information to keep the layer's output close to the original.
Activation-aware weight quantisation: it scales up the weight channels that matter most, as judged by activation size, before rounding to 4 bits.
A small sample of representative inputs run through a model to collect the statistics a quantisation method needs.
Two 8-bit floating-point formats: E4M3 has more precision and less range, E5M2 has more range and less precision.
Quantising only the weights while activations stay in 16 bits, with weights dequantised inside the matrix-multiply kernel.
